headline: Union Rout Cincy 5-0; Road Teams Win Six of 14
dek: Philadelphia's demolition of FC Cincinnati headlined a wild midweek round that saw visitors collect six victories.
body: Philadelphia crushed FC Cincinnati 5-0 at Subaru Park, the sharpest result of a 14-game slate split across Sept. 9-10. Road teams won six times in all. Orlando City took three points from Atlanta 3-2, Charlotte edged Montréal 2-1, Columbus fell at D.C. United 2-1, and Nashville lost at Toronto 2-1 despite holding the East's top record. Vancouver thumped LA Galaxy 3-0, LAFC beat Red Bull New York 2-0, and Houston held off Real Salt Lake 2-1. FC Dallas won at Minnesota 2-1. Austin-Colorado and Chicago-Inter Miami each finished 1-1; Portland and St. Louis drew 2-2; San Jose edged San Diego 3-2.

headline: Rapids Restock Attack; Three Players Leave MLS
dek: Colorado added two European wingers at window's close while three clubs confirmed outbound transfers.
body: Colorado Rapids signed English winger Morgan Whittaker from Middlesbrough on a Designated Player deal and added Ghanaian winger Ibrahim Sadiq from AZ Alkmaar. Charlotte FC's Kerwin Vargas, who logged 1,230 minutes this season, joined Athletico Paranaense of Brazil's Série A on a permanent transfer. Philadelphia Union's Olwethu Makhanya, 1,170 minutes played in 2026, moved to Rangers FC in the Scottish Premiership. Portland Timbers' Felipe Mora, 1,050 minutes this season, joined Liga MX side Atlético de San Luis.

headline: Musa Leads Boot Race at 18; Evander Doubles Up
dek: FC Dallas's striker sits four clear at the top while FC Cincinnati's creator holds joint leads in two columns.
body: Petar Musa of FC Dallas leads the Golden Boot race with 18 goals, four ahead of the next pack. Evander of FC Cincinnati and D.C. United's Tai Baribo both sit on 14. In assists, Evander is joint-top alongside San Diego FC's Anders Dreyer, each at 10. Son Heung-Min of LAFC is third with nine. Evander's dual 10-and-14 line makes him the closest thing to a one-man race in the creative column. Houston's Guilherme is the sharpest finisher by xG, scoring 13 goals against an expected total of 6.4, a gap of plus-6.6.

headline: Nashville Lead East by Distance; Whitecaps Top West
dek: Goal difference is doing as much talking as points as both conference leaders look locked in.
body: Nashville SC lead the Eastern Conference with 53 points on a 16W-5D-3L record. Their 48 goals scored and 19 conceded give them the league's best defense. Vancouver Whitecaps top the West with 46 points at 14W-4D-5L, having scored 52 and conceded 21. Inter Miami CF own the league's best attack with 59 goals for. Nashville's 19 goals against is the stingiest mark in MLS, nine better than the Whitecaps, who backed that defensive record with a 3-0 win over LA Galaxy on Sept. 10.

headline: Dallas edges SKC in seven-goal thriller; Portland tops nine
dek: A week of high-scoring results capped a run of 28 matches across the Eastern and Western conferences.
body: FC Dallas beat Sporting Kansas City 4-3 on Sept. 6 in the week's most eventful result. Portland also put on a show, edging Minnesota United 5-4 the same night. Toronto FC and Chicago Fire split eight goals in a 4-4 draw on Sept. 5, while Columbus routed Colorado 3-0. Philadelphia hammered CF Montréal 2-0 on the 5th, then put five past FC Cincinnati on the 9th. Vancouver blanked LA Galaxy 3-0 on Sept. 10, while LAFC shut out Red Bull New York 2-0 the same night. Three matches across the fortnight finished 0-0.

headline: Three out, three in as window closes on MLS rosters
dek: D.C., Atlanta, and Vancouver each lost a player while Cincinnati and Atlanta added bodies before the deadline.
body: D.C. United permanently transferred forward Jacob Murrell to Falkirk FC of the Scottish Premiership; he logged 870 minutes this season. Atlanta United moved defender Pedro Amador to Hapoel Be'er Sheva of the Israeli Premier League after 960 minutes of 2026 action. Vancouver Whitecaps transferred midfielder Sebastian Berhalter to Middlesbrough FC of the English Championship, where he logged 1,200 minutes this season. On the inbound side, Atlanta signed Argentine midfielder Giuliano Galoppo on loan from River Plate through June 2027. FC Cincinnati added Argentine center-back Julián Malatini on loan from Werder Bremen and Czech midfielder David Douděra from SK Slavia Prague.

headline: Musa and Messi locked at 18, Evander trails by four
dek: FC Dallas and Inter Miami share the lead with four months of regular season behind them.
body: Petar Musa of FC Dallas and Leo Messi of Inter Miami CF each sit on 18 goals, making the Golden Boot race a straight two-horse contest at the top. Evander of FC Cincinnati is third on 14. Messi also leads the assist standings on 11, with Evander and Anders Dreyer of San Diego FC level on 10 apiece. In tackling volume, Vancouver's Andrés Cubas is well clear of the field at 97, with D.C. United's Silvan Hefti second on 60 and teammate João Peglow third on 56.

headline: Nashville leads East with 53 pts; Whitecaps pace West on 46
dek: Nashville's defense and Vancouver's attack give each club a distinct identity at the top of their respective conferences.
body: Nashville SC hold the Eastern Conference lead with 53 points on a 16W-5D-3L record. They have conceded only 19 goals, the best defensive mark in MLS. In the West, Vancouver Whitecaps top the table with 46 points at 14W-4D-5L after their 3-0 win over LA Galaxy on Sept. 10. Inter Miami CF own the league's most productive attack with 59 goals scored, 11 more than second-place Vancouver's 52 across the full league.

headline: FC Dallas edges SKC 4-3 in week's wildest finish
dek: Fourteen matches across four days produced nine goals in Portland alone and a 4-4 thriller in Toronto.
body: Columbus rolled Colorado 3-0 on Sept. 5, the week's most clinical result. Orlando held San Diego 1-0 and Philadelphia turned away CF Montréal 2-0 the same night. Toronto and Chicago traded four goals apiece in a draw. FC Dallas beat Sporting Kansas City 4-3 on Sept. 6, Portland edged Minnesota 5-4, and St. Louis stunned Vancouver 3-1. Inter Miami and Atlanta drew 2-2, Real Salt Lake and LAFC shared the points 2-2, and LA Galaxy topped New England 2-1. Austin and San Jose drew 1-1, Seattle and New York held 0-0, and New York City and Nashville finished goalless on Sept. 4.

headline: Columbus, Vancouver busy as window shuts
dek: Three departures, three arrivals, and the Crew lead the league's late activity heading into the final stretch.
body: Manu García has left Sporting Kansas City after the club mutually terminated his contract; he logs 1,470 minutes this season. Reports link him to a return to Aris Thessaloniki. Hugo Cuypers departs Chicago Fire after 990 minutes in 2026, transferred to Liga MX side CF Monterrey. Chris Cappis exits FC Dallas with 1,080 minutes this season. On the inbound side, Vancouver add forward Yadaly Diaby from French Ligue 2 side Grenoble Foot 38. Columbus bring in winger Anass Zaroury on loan from Panathinaikos and Uruguayan midfielder Santiago Rodríguez.

headline: Musa and Messi locked at 18 goals apiece
dek: FC Cincinnati's Evander sits third at 14, five back, with the assist title also in play.
body: Petar Musa of FC Dallas and Leo Messi of Inter Miami CF are deadlocked at 18 goals, the league's outright leaders. FC Cincinnati's Evander trails at 14. In the assists race, Evander, Messi, and Anders Dreyer of San Diego FC are level at 10 apiece. Andrés Cubas of Vancouver Whitecaps leads all tacklers at 90, more than 30 clear of D.C. United's Silvan Hefti at 59 and teammate João Peglow at 55. On the finishing side, Guilherme of Houston and NYCFC's Nicolás Fernández each outperform their xG by 5.8 goals. St. Louis pair Rafael Navarro and Simon Becher are the league's most prominent under-performers, down 4.3 and 3.5 goals respectively against expectation.

headline: Nashville lead East by a distance; Whitecaps top West
dek: The Eastern leader has allowed just 17 goals all season, also the best defensive record in the league.
body: Nashville SC sit atop the Eastern Conference with 53 points on a 16W-5D-2L record, 47 goals scored and 17 conceded. That goals-against total is also the best in the entire league. Vancouver Whitecaps lead the Western Conference at 43 points, record 13W-4D-5L, with 49 goals for and 21 against. Inter Miami CF hold the league's most potent attack with 58 goals scored, 11 more than the next Western side.
